task: Build a lightweight dev-memory CLI layer so users can preserve and reuse agent programming lessons even when not using Koala.
outcome: User runs dev-memory capture to save a Claude CLI failure lesson, dev-memory preflight "delegate reviewer to Claude" shows the lesson before coding, and dev-start claude prints the same preflight guidance plus a finish reminder.
facts: Users often accumulate workflow, failure-mode, and success-pattern knowledge in normal Claude/Codex/Gemini chats outside Koala.
If that knowledge stays only in chat context, the next agent session will not reliably read or reuse it.
When a Koala story is active, lessons should be linked to story evidence as candidates, not promoted to gate evidence.
INIT reviewers passed B-ad2c with advisory requirements for concrete examples, measurable preflight size, explicit dedupe behavior, and a shared active-story detection primitive.
constraints: Do not make experience memory a Koala DONE gate receipt or substitute for signed evidence.
First version must stay simple: JSONL/Markdown and CLI output, no vector database or UI.
Preflight output must be concise: maximum 5 entries and maximum 60 rendered lines by default.
Duplicate handling must be warn-and-link: write the new entry but include relatedEntryIds and a duplicate warning in output.
Active story detection is shared: prefer explicit --storyId, then KOALA_STORY_ID, then current Koala session/story context from cwd.
unknowns: Exact existing CLI registry files and command naming conventions must be inspected before implementation.
Whether project memory should default inside repository .koala/dev-memory or external user home must be decided in code after inspecting config helpers.
Whether wrappers should execute agent binaries or prompt-only dry-run by default must align with existing safety conventions.
